## [`Docs/Plans/UniverseOverseer.md`](../Plans/UniverseOverseer.md)

| Gate | Decision | Blocks |
|---|---|---|
| C1 | **The overseer's project.** `OutpostOverseer`, a Win32 executable with a row of its own in ADR-002's table, including NeuronCore, NeuronClient, GameProtocol and GameApp; its model and layout in GameApp, tested in GameAppTests. Proposed: as written. The alternative moves the HUD's painter and measured text down into NeuronClient first, so that the overseer does not include GameApp. | OV3, the overseer |
| C2 | **A new token, written by the server.** New token makes a seat's token afresh, writes it into `Universe.json` and writes the seat's join file again, where ADR-078 decision 2 has the server only read its settings. Proposed: yes, written to a new file and renamed into place, as a save is; or New token stays out of the first version. | OV5, the actions |
| C3 | **Dropping a link.** Drop link and Hand to deputy become one action, with an option for the deputy to take the seat at once rather than after ADR-079's minute. The game reads a new close reason, `DroppedByOwner`, as one it does not join again after (ADR-078 decision 10), and goes back to the menu saying the server's owner closed the connection. Proposed: as written. | OV5, the actions |
| C4 | **Full sight on the record.** The universe log writes `overseer <tick> opened` and `closed`, so a friend can see when the owner had full sight open. Proposed: yes. | OV2, the channel |
| C5 | **Packaged or not.** Proposed: not packaged, as `OutpostServer`, so it runs beside the server on a VM without registering a package. | OV3, the overseer |
| C6 | **A server without a GPU.** Proposed: the overseer, and not the game, takes the WARP adapter when no hardware adapter qualifies, which amends ADR-006 decision 6 for it alone; or the overseer always runs from a machine with a GPU. | OV3, the overseer |
| C7 | **A table in the interface.** The style guide has no rule for a table. Proposed: a heading sorts on a click and shows the sort's direction, the picked row takes the picked card's face and edge, and a cell holds a figure over a detail line, written into the style guide with the ADR that owns them. | OV3, the overseer |
